1  DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

-2-  NC: 2024:KHC:1766  MFA No. 3914 of 2021  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 03.07.2021 in M.V.C.No.50/2017 passed by the Additional M.A.C.T. and III Addl. District and Sessions Judge,
Ramanagara ('the Tribunal' for short).
2.

entities.text:
M.A.C.T. and III Addl. District and Sessions Judge,
Ramanagara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 28.03.2016 while the petitioner was the pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09/EF-9433 ridden by one Rakshith met with an accident near Hombaiahnadoddi Petrol Bunk, Ramanagara District, hit by Tractor and Trolley bearing No.KA-42/T-3077-78 killing the rider at the spot and injuring the petitioner.
After taking treatment at NIMHANS and Abhaya Hospital, the petitioner approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.10 lakhs.
Claim was opposed by NC: 2024:KHC:1766 the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence, placing reliance on the judgment of this Court in The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Naresh Babu N. and Another rendered in M.F.A.No.7074/2016 dismissed the claim petition.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Naresh Babu N. and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.R.G.Halesha, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.K.N.Srinivasa,
learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is a pillion rider in the motor cycle in question; the rider since died at the spot, his dependants have filed the claim petition before the very same Tribunal numbered in M.V.C.No.217/2016 which came to be disposed of on 30.05.2018 assessing the compensation.
The said appeal has reached finality before this Court in M.F.A.No.7206/2018 DD 28.05.2021.

When the said NC: 2024:KHC:1766 case has reached finality before this Court and the dependants of the rider were awarded compensation, the Tribunal is wrong in making any assumption and presumption in dismissing the claim petition and he sought for assessment of compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the accident has occurred since both the rider and pillion rider were not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
The Tribunal has rightly relied upon the judgment of this Court in M.F.A.No.7074/2016 (supra) and dismissed the claim petition and he has supported the impugned judgment.

Sri. Raghukumar @ Cheluvaraju vs Sri. Rangaswamy on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82122450/
2 7.

entities.text: Sri. Raghukumar @ Cheluvaraju vs Sri. Rangaswamy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner as pillion rider and death of the rider.
The claim petition filed in M.V.C.No.217/2016 was not NC: 2024:KHC:1766 brought to the knowledge of the Tribunal.
If the judgment dated 30.05.2018 passed has been brought to the notice of the Tribunal, the adverse finding by the Tribunal could not have been happened.
In view of the dependants of the rider have been awarded compensation and confirmed by this Court, the Tribunal cannot record contrary finding to that effect.
Since the accident and cause of the accident is determined, the only question that remains for the Tribunal is to assess the compensation.
9. On careful perusal of the impugned judgment, it is seen that the Tribunal did not assess the compensation and simply dismissed the claim petition.
Hence, the matter requires re-consideration by the Tribunal and it is a fit case for remand.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result,
the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC:1766 ii) The impugned judgment and award is set aside.
iii) The claim petition is restored to the file of Tribunal with a request to the Tribunal to afford an opportunity to the parties to lead evidence, assess the compensation and to decide the case on merits in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible;
iv) Without further notice, the parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 04th March 2024;
vi) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
